findings_to_judge.finding: UNFI's largest customer decelerated inside UNFI's Q4 window: Amazon's 'Physical stores' net sales (mostly Whole Foods) grew 3.6% YoY in Q2 2026 ($5,794mm vs $5,595mm) versus 4.6% in Q1 2026 ($5,785mm vs $5,533mm) — and the Q2 2025 base was itself the quarter of the June 2025 UNFI cyber outage that produced documented Whole Foods out-of-stocks, so the true underlying deceleration is worse than 100bp.

The initial FY2027 guidance at this print will be delivered by a CFO who started on 2026-08-10 — day 29 of his tenure and nine days after the fiscal year closed — as the fifth element of an eight-week C-suite reshuffle that includes an entirely unannounced departure: Matthew Echols ceased serving as Chief Corporate Affairs Officer effective 2026-08-24, disclosed only in an exit Form 4 filed 2026-08-27 with no press release and no 8-K.

UNFI's ~$330mm FY2026 free cash flow guide contains at least $40mm of one-off cyber insurance cash already banked through Q3 ($20mm in Q3 alone, 'included within Operating expenses'), which management itself strips out of adjusted EBITDA via a ($18mm) YTD 'Cybersecurity incident' reconciliation line — while the December 2025 framework anchors FCF at only '~$300 million annually from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028'.

Nine days after the -10.3% Q3 reaction, UNFI's lenders repriced its term loan 75bp tighter — Amendment No. 5, dated 2026-06-18, cut the SOFR margin from 4.75% to 4.00% on ~$371mm outstanding with 'all of the other material terms' unchanged, i.e. no covenant relief was needed.

US Foods' CFO said on 2026-08-13 that his fuel surcharge recovery rate ran "more like 70% for the quarter" versus "our typical 30%, 40%", turning an expected 2% fuel headwind into "less than half of that", explicitly because high diesel "triggered additional customer surcharges that normally only activate at elevated price levels" - the same tiered-surcharge mechanism UNFI described on 2026-06-09 as "contractual protection to share some of the fuel pressures with our customers", in a quarter that overlaps UNFI's 13 weeks to 2026-08-01.

UNFI's 2022 Repurchase Program - $200m authorised 2022-09-21 for a four-year term, so its term runs out this month - still had approximately $109m unused as of 2026-05-02, equal to about 4.2% of the $2.6bn market cap, while net leverage is already at 2.5x heading to ~2.3x against a stated <=2.5x-by-FY26 target and the last buys were struck at $33.66 (Q2) versus $43.94 spot.

The Q4 bar the wire will print at 6:30am - $7.6bn revenue, $0.62 adjusted EPS - is asymmetric against UNFI's own narrowed FY26 guide: $31.1-31.3bn sales less $23.51bn of 39-week actuals implies Q4 sales of $7.59-7.79bn, so $7.6bn sits at the floor of the guided band, whereas $2.40-2.60 adjusted EPS less $1.95 YTD implies Q4 of $0.45-0.65 and $0.62 sits at the ~85th percentile.

The first FY27 guide has to be set against a fuel base far above FY26's with only partial hedging, and UNFI's own multi-year frame gives it cover to guide flat: EIA weekly diesel was $5.599/gal on 2026-08-31 versus $3.708 a year earlier (+51%), the fiscal-Q1-to-date August average is $5.46 versus $3.74 (+46%), and against FY24 adjusted EBITDA of $518m the published "low-double-digit average annual Adjusted EBITDA growth from FY24 to FY27" target is satisfied by FY27 of roughly $690-730m - i.e. flat to +5% on the FY26 guide midpoint of $695m - even though the longer-term algorithm management talks to is high-single-digit EBITDA growth.

The executive who will deliver UNFI's first FY27 guidance started five weeks ago: the 2026-07-09 8-K appointed Alfredo Luchini CFO effective 2026-08-10 (from Carrier Climate Solutions Americas), moved Matteo Tarditi from President/CFO to President/COO, elevated Louis Martin to Chief Commercial Officer and disclosed Mark Bushway's exit - and a fifth change, Matt Echols ceasing to be Chief Corporate Affairs Officer effective 2026-08-24, was disclosed only in a Form 4 remark filed 2026-08-27, with no Item 5.02 8-K, no press release and no trade-press coverage.
